FAILED at fixture setup: 'list matrix_browser_a: 403 permission.denied'. Diagnosis (reproduced by hand): the fixture logs the platform admin in with tenantId=101; under the isolation model a session carrying a tenant claim resolves its roles inside that tenant, so the platform admin - who owns no tenant role - gets an empty role set and every console call is refused. The spec bodies use the same login-for-tenant helper, so they would fail the same way. This is a stale-fixture condition (the fixtures were written before task 2026-10-13-tenant-true-isolation changed the subject model), not a product regression: the sanctioned path - provision a real tenant with POST /system/tenant, then log in as that tenant's own admin - is exactly what tenant-viewpoint-switcher.spec.ts does and it passes 5/5. Fix path recorded in knownGaps.

knownGaps: TENANT HOSTILE MATRIX IS RED AND IS A STALE FIXTURE, NOT A PRODUCT BUG. frontend/scripts/tenant-matrix-fixture-setup.mjs and the three tenant-hostile/tenant-protected spec files log the platform `admin` in with an explicit tenantId against tenants 101/202. Before task 2026-10-13-tenant-true-isolation the platform admin's global /api/v1/* policy still applied inside the tenant; now a tenant-claim session resolves roles inside the tenant (contract §4), so a platform admin with no tenant-scoped role gets an empty role set and 403 permission.denied. Evidence: hand curl of POST /auth/login {username:admin,password:123456,tenantId:101} returns 200 with roles:[] and perms containing platform:dashboard:*, and the very next GET /system/dict/type/list returns code 403 permission.denied. Fix path (not done here, deliberately): provision each fixture tenant through POST /system/tenant so it owns a real tenant_admin (roles + Casbin policies are then written in-process, so the running enforcer sees them), then log in as that tenant's admin - the pattern tenant-viewpoint-switcher.spec.ts already uses and which passes. Doing this needs a reload-or-provision decision for the running backend, which is why it was not rushed into a closeout pass. The CI job smoke-tenant is continue-on-error (advisory), so this has been invisible to merge gates.

PLATFORM ADMIN + TENANT CLAIM = EMPTY ROLE SET. Related to the item above and worth a product ruling: a platform-capable subject that names a tenant at login (or picks one from the picker) ends up in a console it cannot use, because its roles are resolved tenant-scoped. Today this is unreachable in the acceptance state because the platform admin has no memberships after cleanup, but the login picker will offer a platform admin's member tenants and then hand back a session with no authority. Whether a platform-capable subject should retain platform roles inside a tenant claim is a contract-level product decision, not something this pass should decide.
